name: BTS716GBXUMA1
title: BTS716G smart high-side power switch, four channels of 140 mΩ, with status feedback
summary: Four protected high-side switches for 12 V and 24 V grounded loads, built as two chips of two channels in one PG-DSO-20 package with a common Vbb leadframe. Each channel is an N-channel vertical MOSFET with charge pump, a CMOS-level input, current limiting, thermal shutdown with restart, a 47 V inductive clamp, and open-load detection in the off state; each pair of channels reports faults on one open-drain status pin. Channels can be paralleled down to 35 mΩ. It is AEC qualified and RoHS compliant.

circuits.title: Overvoltage and reverse-battery protection
circuits.description: One channel of the switch with the outside resistors that let it survive load dump and a reversed battery. RGND in the ground lead limits the current into the GND pin when the supply goes above the internal clamp or below ground. The status line is pulled up to the 5 V logic rail through one RST and reaches the controller through a second RST, which also limits the current into the ST pin. The input is driven directly. The load returns to load ground; the logic ground is separate.

operation.text: Two identical chips share one leadframe, which is the Vbb connection (pins 1, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 19, 20). Chip 1 holds channels 1 and 2 with ground GND1/2 and status ST1/2; chip 2 holds channels 3 and 4 with GND3/4 and ST3/4. Each channel is an N-channel vertical power MOSFET with its own charge pump, gate control, current limit, inductive clamp, temperature sensor and open-load detector.

Each input is referred to its chip's ground and goes through an internal resistor RI (2.5 to 6.0 kΩ) to a Schmitt trigger and a 6.1 V typ ESD zener; a current sink draws the input current. Above 2.5 V the channel is on, below 1.0 V it is off. The ESD zeners are not meant to clamp DC levels. With RGND fitted, its drop adds to the thresholds.

ST1/2 and ST3/4 are open-drain outputs, each shared by the two channels of its chip, with an ESD zener of 6.1 V typ (0.3 mA max). The on resistance RST(ON) is below 375 Ω at 1.6 mA. The pin is high in normal operation and goes low for an open load in the off state or an overtemperature shutdown in the on state, per the truth table.

Open load is detected only with the channel off: with IN low, an output above the open-load detection voltage VOUT(OL) (1.7 V min, 2.8 V typ, 4.0 V max) pulls the status low. The detection circuit has an outside resistor REXT from Vbb to OUT. When IN goes high on an open load the status returns high within td(STon), 10 µs typ; after IN goes low it falls again within td(SToff), 500 µs max.

On a short the channel current is limited to IL(lim) (9 A typ at 25 °C) and the chip heats until it reaches Tjt, 150 °C min, which turns the channel off after toff(SC), 2 ms typ from a 25 °C start; heating may take several milliseconds depending on conditions. It restarts after cooling by the 10 K hysteresis, so a lasting short cycles at the repetitive limit IL(SCr), 6.5 A typ. The status pin goes low while the channel is held off by temperature, at least 30 µs after IN goes high, and returns high within 20 µs after IN goes low. The other channel of the chip carries on normally.

Channels 1 and 2 (or 3 and 4) work in parallel by joining their inputs and their outputs. To run all four in parallel, ST1/2 and ST3/4 are tied together as a wired-OR with one pull-up resistor. Paralleled channels share one repetitive short-circuit limit of 6.5 A typ, start a short at twice IL(lim), and the clamp of the lowest-VON(CL) channel usually takes the inductive energy.

At switch-off the output is clamped so that Vbb - VOUT is VON(CL), 47 V typ, and the load's stored energy is dissipated in the switch. The allowed load inductance against load current is given for one channel at Tj,start = 150 °C and Vbb = 12 V; the ratings give 21, 25 and 30 mH for one, two and four channels.

A zener of 47 V typ (Vbb(AZ), 41 V min, 52 V max) sits between Vbb and the logic ground. Above Vbb(AZ) the current into GND and ST must be limited outside the chip; 150 Ω in the ground lead is recommended. The load-dump rating is 60 V (VA = 13.5 V, RI = 2 Ω, td = 400 ms).

Up to 32 V reverse, with 150 Ω in the GND connection. Two 150 Ω resistors, one per chip ground, or a single 75 Ω resistor for both, protect against reverse battery up to the maximum operating voltage. The load current then flows through the MOSFET's body diode (600 mV typ at -2 A, 150 °C) and the load sets its limit; the thermal shutdown does not work with reverse current flowing, and input and status currents must stay within their ratings.

With GND open or pulled up and IN low, the output delivers 2 mA max (Vbb = 32 V). With GND disconnected and IN high, VOUT is about VIN - VIN(T+). If the ground is pulled above VIN - VIN(T+), the channel stays off. No low status is available while VGND is above zero.

If the supply is lost while an inductive load carries current, each switch survives, provided the current stays within the ZL limits. All of that load current then returns via the GND pin, and the board's ground path must be laid out to carry it.
The operating range is 5.5 to 40 V. After the supply sags under 5.5 V, the device holds its switching state for 15 ms as long as the supply stays above Vbb(u so), 4.5 V max.

All four channels have the same timing. An output follows its input once Vbb is applied; status stays high in normal operation. When a lamp is switched on, the load current peaks at the inrush and falls to its steady value, and the status stays high.
